common_name: White Swan Azalea (Knap Hill Parent of 'Aromi Sunstruck')

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade.

directions: White Swan is an English deciduous azalea of the Knap Hill breeding tradition, surviving in the record chiefly through its documented role as a parent: Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama crossed it with the native Rhododendron austrinum to produce the fragrant yellow hybrid 'Aromi Sunstruck,' which carries a refined, wavy-edged flower form credited to this English side of the cross. Consistent with its name and with other white-flowered Knap Hill selections, it is presumed to bear white blooms in large spring trusses, though no independent flower description survives in the sources consulted. Like other large Knap Hill azaleas it grows into an upright, multi-stemmed deciduous shrub. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade, and avoid heavy pruning since flower buds set on the previous year's growth.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Kikoshi is a Japanese Satsuki azalea cultivar documented today mainly as one of the two named parents, alongside 'Onyo', behind the mid-twentieth-century Satsuki hybrid 'Fujinami'. No independent description of its own flower color or size survives in the sources consulted, a common gap among older Satsuki parent clones overshadowed by well-known offspring. Like other Satsuki selections it would be expected to flower later in the season than Kurume or Southern Indica azaleas on a compact, small-leaved evergreen shrub. Grow in acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and prune only right after bloom since next year's buds set soon afterward.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Onyo is a Japanese Satsuki azalea cultivar known today chiefly as the second named parent, alongside 'Kikoshi', of the hybrid 'Fujinami' from the early-to-mid twentieth century flowering of Satsuki breeding in Japan. Sources consulted give no independent record of Onyo's own flower color, size, or growth habit, a frequent gap for Satsuki parent clones whose offspring became better known than the parents themselves. As with other Satsuki selections it would be expected to flower later in spring than Kurume or Southern Indica types, on a compact, small-leaved evergreen shrub. Grow in acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, protecting it from hot afternoon sun, and prune only right after bloom.

common_name: Balls of Fire Azalea (Parent of 'Pirate's Booty')

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade.

directions: Balls of Fire is a named selection from Dr. Eugene Aromi's deciduous azalea breeding program in Mobile, Alabama, remembered today mainly for its documented role in parentage: it was combined with 'Cecile' in a complex Aromi seedling that was later crossed with 'Frontier Red' to produce the unscented, bold two-tone hybrid 'Pirate's Booty'. Its fiery name suggests a hot red-to-orange flower tone consistent with that offspring's deep red flush, though no independent description of its own bloom survives in the sources consulted. Like other Aromi hybrids it combines native Gulf South azalea heritage with Exbury parentage for strong heat and humidity tolerance on a medium to large deciduous shrub. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow roots through summer heat.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade.

directions: Persian Melon is one of Dr. Eugene Aromi's named deciduous azalea selections, documented today chiefly as the seed parent of 'Gene's Gold' when crossed with an unnamed Aromi breeding line selection. Its melon-evoking name and the creamy gold, rose-tipped flowers it passed on to that offspring both point toward warm orange-to-gold flower tones, though no independent description of its own bloom survives in the sources consulted. Like other Aromi hybrids it combines native Gulf South azalea parentage with Exbury breeding for strong heat and humidity tolerance on a medium to large deciduous shrub. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow roots through Gulf Coast summer heat.

directions: Gillian's Gold is a named selection from Dr. Eugene Aromi's deciduous azalea breeding line, documented today chiefly as a parent crossed with an unnamed Aromi seedling to produce 'Indian Yellow', which carries large light yellow flowers shaded bright red. Its own name points to a golden flower color in keeping with other yellow-flowered Aromi introductions, though no independent description of its own bloom survives in the sources consulted. Like other Aromi hybrids it draws Gulf Coast heat and humidity tolerance from native azalea parentage crossed with Exbury breeding stock, on a medium to large deciduous shrub. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow roots through hot summers.

directions: Sunbeam is a named selection from Dr. Eugene Aromi's deciduous azalea breeding program in Mobile, Alabama, documented today chiefly as a parent crossed with an unnamed breeding-line selection to produce 'April Yellow', a bright yellow-flowered introduction. Its sunny name is consistent with a yellow-to-gold flower color, matching the pattern of other Aromi parents whose names anticipate the color they pass on, though no independent description of Sunbeam's own bloom survives in the sources consulted. Like other Aromi hybrids it combines native Gulf South azalea heritage with Exbury parentage for strong heat and humidity tolerance on a medium to large deciduous shrub. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow roots through summer heat.

common_name: Taihai Satsuki Azalea (Parent of the Dwarf Sport 'Kazan')

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Taihai is a Japanese Satsuki azalea cultivar documented today chiefly as the parent clone from which the ultra-dwarf, tiny-leaved sport 'Kazan' arose, a mutation prized separately for shohin bonsai. No independent description of Taihai's own flower color or mature size survives in the sources consulted, a common gap for Satsuki parent clones whose sports became better known in cultivation than the original plant. Like other standard-sized Satsuki selections it would be expected to flower later in spring than Kurume or Southern Indica azaleas on a compact, small-leaved evergreen shrub. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and prune or pinch only right after flowering to preserve next year's buds.
